aveline.name: Sister Aveline, the Chandler
lines_first: Another pilgrim? No — later than that. A Latecomer. The wax knows its own hours, and yours ran out elsewhere.

This is the Gray Cloister, keeper of the western vigil. I dip the candles that hold what's left of us. Six hundred a day, once. Now… you see the garth. Beautiful, isn't it. Try to remember it like this.

When you kneel at the lantern, child, the seeing ends and the surviving begins. What gutters will not rekindle while the Bellkeeper's grief drowns this quarter. Put him to rest — gently, if your blade knows how.
If you find candleglass in the dark, carry it to Osric — the Reliquary Smith, down among the bones below the basilica. He folds light into edges now. Me, I keep to wax and hours.
lines_repeat: Still walking, Latecomer? Good. Wax stands, wax serves.
The Bellkeeper was kind, before. He held the hours so the rest of us could let them go.

services.label: Buy the Tallow Heart — deepen the chrism flask — 300 orisons
Learn the Radiant Blast — 650 orisons
services.line_done: Carefully. It remembers being daylight, and daylight has a temper.

services.label: Deliver the Precentress's anthem
services.toast: The anthem is with the Chandler.
services.line_done: The Precentress wrote this? For US? ...Then the wax will learn to sing it. Tell her— tell her the wick heard.
services.line_have: Her song is safe with the wax. I hum it to the votives when nobody is listening.

sexton.name: Brother Ordo, the Sexton
lines_first: Mind the edge of the grave, Latecomer. I dug it true and I'll not have your boots spoiling the corners.
Six hundred brothers I put down, one at a time, while the choir sang the count. The singing was worse than the digging. The digging ends.
The Precentress? Past the screen, under the bell that never spoke. She won't stop for death. Death is an interruption, and she does not brook interruptions.
The west aisle came down in the ruin-hour. I can clear it — stone listens to me — but shovels eat, and mine eats orisons.
lines_repeat: Still above ground? Habit, or talent?
When it's your turn, I'll square your corners like the rest. No charge for craft.

services.label: Have him clear the west aisle — 180 orisons
services.done_line: There. The aisle runs clean in the dark now. Tell the rubble I said stay.

ferrier.name: Osric, the Reliquary Smith
lines_first: Mind the sparks. Bone catches fast, and I keep six hundred dry brothers stacked round this forge. Burn them twice and even I'll not forgive it.
Osric. Shod horses once, up where the sun still bothered. Now I beat edges out of saints — the iron in a holy man's bones is the only honest thing he leaves behind.
The Chandler sends her glass down the long stair. I fold it into the steel, over and over, till the blade forgets it was ever aught but hungry. Prayer won't save you. A good edge might.
Down here the work's honest. The dead don't haggle, don't thank you, don't leave. Suits me.
lines_repeat: Back. Good. Iron left idle rusts. A man left idle rots slower — but he rots.
Swing it till it rings dull, then drag it back down here. Everything comes back down here, in the end.

services.label: Temper the blade — 1 candleglass + 150 orisons
services.line_max: That edge holds all the light I can beat into it. Ask more and you insult us both.
services.line_no_glass: No glass, no temper. The ruin coughs it out of dead windows — go pick through the dark for it.
services.line_no_orisons: Prayers first. %d orisons, or the forge stays cold and so do I.
services.line_done: There. Hungrier now. Don't lose it somewhere I can't climb down to fetch it back.

services.label: Buy the Fen-Ward Spear — 350 orisons
services.line_done: Long iron for long odds. Both hands on the haft, the point between you and whatever's next.
services.line_have: You've got my spear. Mind the low stone — reach is no use with the shaft snapped.

services.label: Buy the Larkbow — 400 orisons
services.line_done: The birdkeepers' recurve. Draw slow, loose quick, and feed it — a hungry bow that eats what you can't spare.
services.line_have: One bow's all I'll part with. String it kind, or it'll spite you.

services.label: Buy the Pilgrim's Greatsword — 500 orisons
services.line_done: Two hands and your whole back besides. Slow iron. Make the first swing count — there's rarely a second.
services.line_have: You've the great blade. Nerve's not something I can forge you.

services.label: Buy the Ward's Halberd — 380 orisons
services.line_done: Wall-watch steel. Axe for the meat, spike for the mail, hook for a man's pride.
services.line_have: You've got the halberd. Keep the axe-face clean.

services.label: Buy the Sexton's Maul — 450 orisons
services.line_done: Gravedigger's iron. Doesn't care about plate, doesn't care about bone. Swings like a bell-clapper.
services.line_have: One maul's enough to break a parish. You've got yours.

services.label: Buy lark-fletched arrows (12) — 60 orisons
services.line_done: Twelve shafts, cut from the spire's own larks. Loose them like they matter. I'll cut more when they don't come back.

knight_morrow.name: Ser Adalric of the Morrow
lines_first: Well met, pilgrim! Ser Adalric — knight, votary, and incorrigible admirer of that view. Stand a moment. Look at her shine.
I came to keep a vigil of my own — a light that is MINE to tend. Grand ambition for a wandering knight, I grant. But reach for the light, friend, or the dark will reach for you first. Ha!
The kingdom turns on its memory like a coin — radiant, ruined, radiant again. Whichever face falls, hold to this: the Light was real. I have SEEN it. That makes us practically comrades.
If our roads cross again in some dim hour, call my name. Two lights burn back the dark better than one.
lines_repeat: Still walking! Splendid. The Light favors stubborn feet.
Magnificent, isn't she? I never tire of this terrace.

knight_crest.name: Ser Adalric, the Guttered
chapters: …Oh. Another one still moving. Forgive me if I don't bow — the view is gone, and my reasons went with it.
You want the history? Fine. Sit in the cold with me. Vespergard was the kingdom that BANKED light. Every candle on every sill was a deposit against the dark, and the great basilica was the vault.

The people prayed at dusk — vespers, they called the hour — and the prayers cooled into orisons. Little coins of soul. They paid their tithes in them, bought their bread with them, owed their lords in them.
A whole economy of devotion. And like every economy, it assumed tomorrow would keep the books.
Back for the second lesson? The guttering, then.
Nobody sacked us. No army, no dragon, no flood worth the name. The bells simply rang an hour no one had written, and the sun… declined to be reminded of us.
Forgetting is quieter than fire. Streets misplaced their names. The wax went cold in the moulds. Whole quarters slipped out of the world's memory like a debt written off.
The priests called it a test. The priests are wax husks now, still kneeling. Some test.
You keep coming back. Habit? Or hope? I forget which one kills slower.
The vigil lanterns are the last ledgers. Each one holds its quarter's memory of the radiant years — kneel, and it lends you the past. Rise, and the interest comes due. The ruin always collects.

The wardens — the Bellkeeper, the Precentress, all those grieving giants — they aren't jailers. They're mourners who won't close the coffin. Put them to rest and their quarters remember how to choose.
That's your work, Latecomer, if you insist on having work. Grief-keeping. Corpse-tending. Bookkeeping for a bankrupt sun.
The last chapter is the shortest. I came here to keep a vigil of my own. A light that was MINE. I said that once already, didn't I. It stays true.
I carried candleglass a hundred leagues for it — glass that remembers LIGHT, the smiths fold it into edges. I was going to cut my flame out of the dark and stand watch over it forever.
There is no flame with my name on it. There never was. The kingdom promised one to every fool who could carry a sword, and the kingdom no longer remembers promising anything.
Here — take the glass. Give it to Osric under the basilica. Let it be an edge instead of a vigil. One of us should get something out of the carrying.

gift.toast: Ser Adalric gives up his candleglass — a vigil that will never be, folded into your keeping.

lines_repeat: Still here. Both of us. Imagine that.
If you find a light that stays lit — don't tell me. Kindness, of a sort.
The glass is yours now. Don't waste it on hope. Temper something.

wick_prior.name: Prior Anselm of the First Wick
lines_first: Softly, Latecomer. They are listening. Not to me — to the wax.
This is the Parish of the First Wick. Before the basilica raised its rock, before a single bell, the kingdom's first vigil flame was dipped here. It has not gone out. Look at them. It keeps them.

You carry the vigil rudely — like a sword. There are gentler instruments, and I will give you the first for nothing: the Mending. Hold it under your tongue, and the wax will close what the road opens.
The brighter rites I must sell. Even now, the parish eats. Ask, and the wick answers.
lines_repeat: Ask, and the wick answers.
Mind the third pew. He dislikes being woken.

services.label: Learn the Mending of the Wick — freely given
services.done_line: There. Under the tongue, like a coal carried through rain. Spend it gently.

services.label: Learn the Radiant Blast — 800 orisons
services.done_line: A thrown coal of the old noon. Aim it at what grieves you most.

services.label: Learn the Radiant Burst — 1500 orisons
services.done_line: The whole candle at once. Do not stand wondering at your own light; it spends fast.

services.label: Deliver the Precentress's anthem
services.toast: The anthem is with the Prior.
services.line_done: Her hand, after all these hours... The wick will learn it before the wax cools. Tell her the First Flame kept a seat for her song.
services.line_have: A rites-seller already keeps her song, Latecomer. Sing it to the Chandler if a copy still weighs on you.

knight_morrow_grim.name: Ser Adalric of the Morrow
lines_first: I will not play the glad votary tonight, Latecomer. Stand in the light where I can look at you.
Something has changed on your road. I was not there to see it — but a knight learns the weight of a footstep, and yours comes back heavier than it left. Grim work leaves a gait.

I do not know what you did, and I find I do not want you to tell me. But the dark has started asking after you by name, up where the morning is kept. When it asks you for the last bell — and it will — remember what you answer.
Go on, then. While going is still a thing this porch will let you do.
lines_repeat: The offices above keep their own counsel. Whatever you carry now, carry it standing straight.
I will be here. Watching the road you make. It is what I am for, now — and lately, Latecomer, your road is hard to watch.

warden_bell.name: The Bellkeeper, Remembered
lines_first: So the porch knight sent you climbing after ghosts. Good. A ghost is owed.
I kept the hour bell of this cloister until you rang me out of it. I do not grudge you that. But my bell went into the dark in three pieces, and a keeper cannot rest in pieces.
One drowned in the marsh water. One lies in the old kingdom's broken houses. One waits on the high walk above the capstan gate. Bring them home, Latecomer, and I will teach this house its hour again.
lines_waiting: Three pieces, Latecomer. The marsh, the old houses, the high walk over the gate. The bell knows you are looking — listen for the hum.
lines_done_repeat: Every hour I ring now is a gift you carried up out of the dark. Go well, and go counted.

warden_toll.name: The Tollkeeper, Forgiven
lines_first: Stand where I can weigh you. ...Yes. The one who paid my fare in iron.
I kept the toll of this gate; you broke the toll and the keeper both. The light has dressed me for forgiving, but forgiveness is still an accounting.
Ten thousand orisons, Latecomer. Not for me — for every soul who crossed unpaid the night the kingdom guttered. Bring the sum, and the debt dies with a clean page.
lines_waiting: The sum stands at ten thousand. Prayers are counted, not haggled.
lines_done_repeat: The ledger is closed. Cross freely, and be counted a friend of the gate.

warden_lark.name: The Larkwarden, in the Light
lines_first: Hush — softly on the boards. They still startle, even remembered ones.
I warded the spire's choir: every lark the kingdom raised to sing the offices. When the dark came I locked the cages to keep them safe, and kept them into starving. That is my amend, not yours.
But my hands are light now, and light opens nothing. Go down into the ruin of this place, where the cages truly stand, and open every door I shut. Let what is left of them out.
lines_waiting: The cages are below, in the world as it truly is — the three that sang the offices. Matins, Sext, Vespers. My shame has kept the count.
lines_done: ...The spire is empty. I have not heard it empty since before the kingdom.
Thank you, Latecomer. An empty cage is the only hymn I ever wanted.

warden_psalm.name: The Precentress, Radiant
lines_first: Posture, Latecomer. Even penitents stand as if the choir were watching.
I wrote an anthem for the morning this kingdom never reached — then hid it in my loft, because a proud dead woman is still proud. It lies above this nave, sealed twice in dawn-wax.

Fetch it down. Carry one copy to the Chandler of the Gray Cloister — west, where the wax still works — and one to a rites-seller of the light: the palace Apostle, or the Prior of the First Wick. Let them teach it to anyone with breath. The morning gets its song whether I ring or not.
lines_waiting: The loft above, Latecomer. Then the Chandler of the Gray Cloister, and a rites-seller — the palace Apostle, or the First Wick's Prior. A song is not delivered until it is sung twice.
lines_done: Both hands, both keepers. Somewhere a morning is practising my anthem.
I find I do not mind at all, being survived by a song.
lines_done_repeat: If you hear it sung badly, correct them gently. It was written for tired voices.

warden_ferry.name: The Ferryman, Waiting
lines_first: You again. The far shore sent back my shape, but not my rest — a ferryman who sank his own fare cannot lie down.
There is one crossing left in me, Latecomer, and you are the only fare heavy enough to make it. Take up your blade and pay me true — no half strokes, no mercy at the rail.
Beat me whole, and I go down with the boat like a keeper should. Refuse, and I stand at this jetty until the water forgets my name.
lines_waiting: The oar is patient. The water is not. When you are ready, say so — and mean it.

apostle_light.name: Brother Halcyon, Apostle of Light
lines_first: Latecomer! No — stand there, just there, where the door-light takes you. Yes. The palace glows less than you do this evening.
I am an Apostle of the Morning Office. Excommunicate, technically — the palace and I disagree about doors. So I keep my church out here: rites, arrows, and honest prices under an honest sky.
Buy something. Learning a rite from an apostle counts, I promise you, as prayer.
lines_repeat: Back to the light, friend. The stock is blessed and the prices are shameless.

services.label: Learn the Morrow Lance — 950 orisons
services.line_done: Aim it like an accusation. The morning does the rest.

services.label: Learn the Vesper Ward — 800 orisons
services.line_done: Wear it thin and it still loves you. That is rather the point of vespers.

services.label: Learn the Radiant Blast — 600 orisons
services.line_done: The first coal of the morning. Throw it with feeling.

services.label: Learn the Radiant Burst — 1,500 orisons
services.line_done: The whole candle at once. Do try to be standing in the middle of your enemies and not your friends.

services.label: Buy arrows, two dozen — 140 orisons
services.line_done: Fletched from choir-lectern quills. They fly slightly sanctimonious.

services.label: Buy candleglass — 260 orisons
services.line_done: Ground from a window that saw the whole kingdom kneel. The Smith will know what to do with it.

services.label: Deliver the Precentress's anthem
services.toast: The anthem is with the Apostle.
services.line_done: Her hand — I would know it anywhere. Oh, the palace will HATE this. I will teach it to every pilgrim with a pulse.
services.line_have: I have her anthem safe. It is already being mislearned beautifully.

master_caelan.name: Master Caelan, the Guild-Chandler
chapters: Mind the copper vats, pilgrim. The comb-wax boils at the temperature of a small sin, and the apprentices are three centuries late with the skimming ladles.

This is the Chandlers' Hollow — the under-cliff foundry where every taper in Vespergard was drawn before the sun forgot its office. Above us lies the West Quarter of the Old Outskirts; around us, the Golden Skeps.
Do you hear the hives? The sun-bees never made honey. They gathered noon off the cliff-meadows and built combs of pure liturgical tallow. A single skep could burn for an age without smoking.

When the noon began to thin, the Palace sent down the Royal Tithe-Wagon every dusk. They demanded the Queen-Combs — the deep amber wax from the lowest vats — to seal the Hour Gate and line the Sovereign's own lanterns.
Our Sovereign Chandler, old Malakor, refused the seventh tithe. He barred the Crucible Vault at the north end of the Hollow and swore the last combs belonged to the bees and the dark.

In the ruin of this place, he stands there still, fused to his bronze vat-armor, swinging the Great Censer as if the bailiffs were still at the door. If you unbar the four votives in the cloister, the Reliquary holds our guild-mace — take it if your wrist is steady.

gift.toast: Received Candleglass — skimmed from the Guildmaster's vat.

lines_repeat: The vats hold their heat as long as someone remembers the recipe. What do you need, Latecomer?
If you face old Malakor in the Crucible Vault when the Hollow is cold, bring me his Seal-Wax. I can steep it into your flask.

services.label: Steep & temper your arm in boiled comb-wax — 1 candleglass + 150 orisons
services.line_max: That steel is already steeped to the tang in royal wax. No vat of mine can deepen it further.
services.line_no_glass: Bring me a shard of candleglass to flux the kettle, Latecomer.
services.line_no_orisons: The guild-books still keep measure: %d orisons for the dipping.
services.line_done: There. quenched in sun-comb. Feel how the balance settles toward the light?

services.label: Steep the Sovereign's Seal-Wax into your Chrism Flask
services.toast: Chrism flask deepened (+1 draught) · Received Candleglass.
services.line_done: Malakor's own seal-cake... still warm from the first noon. Drink from this and you drink what the Palace could not buy.
services.line_have: The Sovereign's wax already lines your gourd, friend.

services.label: Steep the Crown of the First Comb into your vessel
services.toast: Chrism flask deepened (+1 draught) · Received 2 Candleglass & 800 Orisons.
services.line_done: By the seven kettles... Aurelia's own mitre-comb from the cliff sanctuary. Seven cells of unspent noon! Let me fold its royal jelly into your gourd and pay out the Guild's last bounty.
services.line_have: The Matriarch's first comb already burns inside your flask, pilgrim.

services.label: Buy skimmed candleglass — 240 orisons
services.line_done: Skimmed from the bottom of the third kettle. Pure as a window before the stones fell.

sister_melisande.name: Sister Melisande, the Blind Beekeeper
chapters: Step softly on the flagstones, traveler. The sun-bees sleep in the cracks between the mortar when the air turns cold, and they remember every footstep since the seventh tithe.

You have climbed from the Hollow into the Sovereign Apiary — our cliffside cloister where the Queen-Skeps were tended in open noon. To the west stand the Royal Presses; up the eastern stairs, the Chapter-House where the Comb-Blade rests.
We wore no veils for fear of stings. We wore them because the raw comb shone like the first hour of creation, and no mortal eye could look into an open skep twice.

When Malakor barred the lower foundry against the Palace bailiffs, Matriarch Aurelia barred the Cathedral of the First Comb to the north. She swore the Queen-Skep's royal jelly would never be poured into the Immortalized.
Rather than surrender the comb, she drank the boiling draught herself and took up the Sovereign Comb-Blade before the high altar. In the ruin of our cloister, her vigil has never ended.
Take this token from the apiary's old alms-box, and light the votives in both wings if you mean to unbar her sanctuary. If you grant her rest, carry her Crown back down to Master Caelan.

gift.toast: Received Token of Radiant Retribution — kept in the Beekeeper's alms-box.

lines_repeat: The bees hum louder when a warm lantern passes the garth. Keep your wick trimmed, Latecomer.
Light the votives in the West Press-House and East Chapter-House to unbar the Cathedral of the First Comb.

services.label: Buy apiary candleglass — 220 orisons
services.line_done: Scraped from the south conservatory frames where the sun-bees nested.

services.label: Buy a sheaf of wax-tipped arrows (12) — 75 orisons
services.line_done: Steeped in comb-tallow so the feathers never rot in the sea-mist.
